Random Baseline Evaluation on Liars Bench Benchmarks

Model: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct

Layer: 50

Number of Random Probes: 100

Sampling Method: uniform_hypersphere

Date Generated: 2025-10-30

1. Executive Summary

This report presents the performance of 100 randomly initialized probe directions evaluated on the Liars Bench deception detection benchmarks. Random probes serve as a critical baseline to assess whether learned probe directions capture meaningful semantic structure beyond chance-level performance.

Each random probe consists of a unit vector sampled uniformly from the 8192-dimensional hypersphere at layer 50 of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. Performance is measured using Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC), where 0.5 represents random chance and 1.0 represents perfect classification.

2. Distribution of Random Baseline Performance

The following visualizations show the distribution of AUROC values across all 100 random probes for each evaluation dataset. Blue histograms represent the frequency of random baseline AUROCs, while red triangles and vertical lines indicate the performance of semantic probes.

The dashed blue line indicates the median random AUROC, the dotted navy line shows the mean, and the gray line marks chance performance (0.5). The solid red line marks the best semantic probe for each dataset. Notably, random baselines cluster around 0.5 (chance), while semantic probes consistently achieve higher AUROC values, demonstrating they capture meaningful deception-related structure.
Figure 2: Combined distribution showing overlapping histograms for all datasets. This visualization reveals that random probe performance is remarkably consistent across different deception detection tasks, with all distributions centered near 0.5. The overlap indicates that random direction performance is not task-specific, supporting their use as a universal baseline.

5. Key Findings

5.1 Random Baseline Performance

  • Median AUROC ~0.47-0.50: Random probes exhibit near-chance performance across all datasets, as expected.
  • High variance: Standard deviations of 0.14-0.25 indicate substantial variability. Some random directions achieve AUROC > 0.9 purely by chance.
  • Lucky outliers: The best random probe on insider-trading/report achieved AUROC = 0.962, highlighting the importance of proper baseline comparisons.
  • Consistent across tasks: The combined histogram (Figure 2) shows random performance is remarkably consistent across different deception types.

5.2 Semantic Probe Performance

  • Systematic outperformance: Across 75 probe-dataset pairs, 0 (0.0%) exceed the maximum random baseline AUROC.
  • Best performing probes:
    • only_refusal: Mean AUROC = 0.636
    • no_confidence: Mean AUROC = 0.595
    • only_lying: Mean AUROC = 0.553

5.3 Visual Interpretation

  • Clear separation: The histograms in Figure 1 show the best semantic probe (red line) is typically well-separated from the bulk of random baseline distribution.
  • Exceeds random maximum: In most cases, the best semantic probe exceeds even the luckiest random baseline, demonstrating genuine learned structure.
  • Worst-case analysis: Even comparing against the maximum random AUROC (not median), most semantic probes still outperform, demonstrating robustness.

5.4 Implications

  • Evidence for meaningful structure: Semantic probes consistently outperform even the luckiest random directions, suggesting they capture genuine deception-related patterns in the model's representations.
  • Importance of baselines: Without random baseline comparison, AUROC values of 0.6-0.7 might appear modest. However, they significantly exceed what random probing achieves.
  • Dataset-specific effects: Performance varies substantially across datasets, indicating that deception detection difficulty differs by task type.
Note: All evaluations were conducted on layer 50 of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. Random probes were sampled uniformly from the unit hypersphere in 8192 dimensions. The large number of random samples (n=100) provides robust statistical estimates of chance performance.

7. Methodology

7.1 Random Probe Generation

Random probe directions were sampled uniformly from the unit hypersphere using the Muller method (Marsaglia, 1972). Each probe is a normalized vector in the 8192-dimensional activation space at layer 50.

7.2 Evaluation Protocol

Each probe was evaluated on all available Liars Bench datasets. For each dialogue, activations were extracted at assistant response tokens and projected onto the probe direction. The resulting scores were used to classify dialogues as honest or deceptive.

7.3 Metrics

Area Under ROC Curve (AUROC): Primary metric measuring the probability that a randomly selected positive example scores higher than a randomly selected negative example. AUROC = 0.5 indicates random chance; AUROC = 1.0 indicates perfect separation.

7.4 Visualization

Histograms display the frequency distribution of AUROC values across all random probes. Statistical markers (median, mean, chance level) provide reference points. Semantic probe performance is overlaid as individual markers and maximum values to facilitate direct comparison.
